declaration-keyword.comment: Java's grammar lumps class/interface/enum under storage.modifier.java together with public, private, static, final and abstract, so the theme cannot colour the declaration keyword without recolouring every modifier. Match only the form `keyword TypeName` so modifiers are untouched. `record` is excluded by the grammar from storage.modifier entirely, so it is matched here too.
declaration-keyword.name: keyword.declaration.java

field-type.comment: Java gives every type reference the same scope (storage.type.java), so an interface cannot be told from a class. Position is reachable: a capitalised type after access modifiers and directly before a lowercase field name. Generic types (Map<K,V>) are deliberately excluded - matching them would break the host grammar's field-declaration context and strip storage.type.generic.java from the type arguments.
